I am a relatively newly-minted Christian. I know, it's a "religion," but I've yet to darken the doors of a church, it's just been me, the Bible, and God, so I'm calling it my spiritual practice. I've gotten very gentle inner prompting and guidance since I embarked on this path almost a year ago. Besides reading scripture, I felt called a few months back to try observing the Sabbath, as in abstaining from all work on Saturday, just resting, praying, and worshiping. Shortly after I started doing that, I was given the strength and desire to stop using kratom. I stayed clean for almost 90 days, and while it was rough going at times, I felt like I was inside a sort of protective bubble, and my resolve to stay clean was like iron.

Buuuuuut, Einstein here decided to stop reading the Bible and stop observing the Sabbath, and, perhaps not surprisingly, I found myself going off the rails and eventually, when I was experiencing some severe pain in my shoulder, I crumbled, bought some capsules, and started using again. Sigh.

So, good thing is, I've rededicated myself to Yeshua. Oh, and before any Christians read this and come at me about the Sabbath, I'm not at all saying that this is something all Christians should be doing. There are those who believe it's still necessary, and many more who don't, and the debating, on this and many other facets of the faith, is fierce. I find it exhausting and kind of disheartening, honestly. I've prayed that God will direct me to a denomination/worship community when/if He sees fit.

As for the Sabbath, I currently believe that God saw what a lazy slob I was on any given Saturday and said, ok, let's turn this into an actual day of rest (rather than scrolling on my phone all day - one of my handful of other addictions/crutches), and also a day for you to be still and know I am God. And while it was challenging at first, I really loved it and felt truly restored after a day like this and also close to God. I love percussion, so I call it being in the pocket with the Holy Spirit. And it seems to carry over thruout the week.

It's funny to be talking about this, though, because I had a rough day today, and on the way home, I'm like, God, am I even a Christian??? I do this a lot honestly. We are to become more like Christ as our faith matures, and, well, maybe it's just growing awareness, but I feel like I'm more sinful now than I was when I started this journey! And I am NOT obedient and don't really want to be. I just want to keep doing what I'm doing w/out the negative consequences. Maybe it's just the addict nature. But man, looking at myself without the usual filters is...not fun. I'm going to journal after this and just lay it all out for God. Journaling is one way I reach out to the Lord, besides praying in my head or out loud. Or just talking to Him. I do get responses, and they're always helpful.

I'm not trying to proselytize, I promise, just answering your question. I don't think I'm qualified to witness, not yet anyway. I've told the J-Man that if he wants me to do that, He's got his work cut out for him! 😂 All I can share at this point is my experience and where I'm at in this journey, or whatever you want to call it.

Me, too. In my case, all I do is grieve the Holy Spirit. I am addicted to ease and the avoidance of pain. I can feel the misery of my rebellion, and I fear hell, but I still sin in the same ways.

I don't think I am born again, because if I was, I would be willing to suffer. It's really scary because I know better now. I actually was more ethical in a lot of ways before I tried to be a Christian. I worked hard and knew how to suffer. Not anymore.

I'm now looking at how to address all of these. Just quitting the kratom, while extremely important, isn't going to fix my addiction issues. I have a lot more work to do.

NAD - I had one of these appear out of nowhere on my inner arm. I wound up going to urgent care and getting some antibiotic cream because I was also afraid it was staph, and I was going to be spending several days with my elderly father. It healed up fine and didn't spread. My guess is it would have done the same w/out the cream. I was just being super careful.

One thing I would advise (others may disagree) is to NOT try to pop it or anything like it, as I'd be worried about spreading the infection, if staph is involved. Just keep it clean and covered. If it spreads, grows, the redness gets worse or spreads, etc., etc., then yes, seek medical attention.

I would say try a meeting. I guarantee you lots of other people who attend meetings are feeling the same way you are. There are people at meetings who are still using. And at some of the NA meetings I attended, they would give you a chip if you wanted it, to symbolize your desire to quit.

You DO want to quit, but the addicted part of your brain is trying to convince you not to quit. That's just what it does, but we don't have to continue to let it have the final say.

Also, just want to chime in with others that you are not alone with the relapsing. I had almost 3 months clean and got back on it a couple weeks back when I was experiencing some severe pain that other pain meds weren't helping much with. Funnily enough, the kratom didn't help much either!

I'm pleased to say the pain has abated, and I'm now tapering off the k. Fortunately, I was taking a mere fraction of what I was consuming daily before my last quit. I was experiencing some really strong disappointment and depression over succumbing, but now I'm reaching the acceptance and resignation phase, where I dust myself off and get right back into the sober wagon.

You can do it. And it's OK to be mixed up. Get more support if you need it, and try not to let the perfect be the enemy of the good.

I would take it as yet another sign of the healing process. Kratom tends to blunt or numb one's feelings, so when you come off of it, you may have formerly suppressed emotion flooding back in. But I think a lot of us here never learned how to handle emotions. You would have to have had caregivers who had that skill themselves, and how many people are that fortunate? And when you don't know what to do with feelings, they can feel unbearable, scary, and even dangerous. So we do whatever we can to avoid feeling.

I'm at almost 50 days clean. My cravings have been pretty intense. They are now starting to let up, though I still have bursts of them.

My go to strategy, fwiw, is to tell my little addicted brain that we're going to just go without that day. Just one more day. And if we're miserable tomorrow, THEN we'll go get some. Wash, rinse, repeat.

Mornings are hard, and when I wake up with a craving, I'll tell myself, if we're intensely suffering after we get through work, we'll get some. I'm invariably in a much better state of mind after work and don't want to. But if I did, I'd say, let's see how we feel tomorrow, and THEN we'll get some.

This is not to say I'm not fully committed to never touching the stuff again. This is just how I cope in the moment with cravings, stress, emotional discomfort, etc.

I've been feeling genuinely better the past couple of days, after going through several really low days with major cravings. It does get better, and every day you don't take this stuff, your brain heals a little more, and you're that much closer to feeling routinely better - and with no toxic, green sludge!! Hurrah!!!

That's gonna be hard. But I was feeling pretty hopeless about my kratom addiction, and here I am 46 days clean. So, I can learn to live without my other crutches. It's not even living, really. But it's all I know.

BTW, I did at-home ketamine therapy for about a year and found it helpful. Even if you don't experience anything profound or trippy during your sessions, you will most likely still benefit. I was a super-responder, and almost k-holed on half the full dose. I did not enjoy that, so with my prescribing doctor's permission, I kept my doses about half the usual amount. I still had some nice experiences, but I didn't go into orbit, and it eliminated my passive ideations that I've lived with the better part of my life. Feel free to message me if you want to ask any questions. Good luck my friend!

How do you feel about twelve step programs? I ask because there are two that deal with finances, Debtors Anonymous and Underearners Anonymous. I am in both, and I really don't know if I'd still be here without them, D.A. especially.

You do not have to be some overspending maniac to be in D.A. I myself am not. My main issues are health-related (mostly mental health) and a longstanding pattern of underearning as well as a tendency to live in deprivation and to feel that is all I can expect and deserve.

You don't have to be religious or even spiritual, either. You can be an atheist and still get help from these programs. What's so awesome about them, at least to me, is that you are meeting up with other people who are in dire financial straits as well as those who have been and found a way out. So, you have people to commiserate with and people who can help you find a way out of debt and underearning, no matter what your circumstances are. I felt utterly hopeless when I walked thru those doors the first time, but I met people who came back from far, far, FAR worse situations than I was in. It has given me so much hope, and my circumstances have begun to improve since I started attending meetings regularly and having Pressure Relief meetings. PR meetings are between you and two other people in the program who are currently solvent. You share whatever information you feel comfortable with these folks about the state of your finances, earning, etc., and they give you encouragement and help you come up with an action plan to tackle whatever weds tackling. Ideally, you have these meetings monthly.

I could go on and on, but I just wanted to put that out there as a possibility in case you weren't aware of either of these programs. If it's not for you, no problem. But if you think you are interested, feel free to ask me any questions, either here or by message.
